summary: Macro backdrop for ags: mixed (score -1 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates +; dollar 0; brl −; risk 0; energy +; china −; breadth −. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Cheese +15.5%; weakest: Oats -17.0%. Key releases ahead: US Congressional Elections (11-03 10:16 AM ET); US Average Hourly Earnings m/m (11-06 8:30 AM ET); US Non-Farm Employment Change (11-06 8:30 AM ET); US Unemployment Rate (11-06 8:30 AM ET).

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 4.91% (-37 bp in a month), 2-year 4.59% (-24 bp); 2s10s curve +32 bp (-13 bp in a month). Falling yields ease funding costs and support commodity investment flows. T-bill yield 4.03% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 101.87 (-0.1% in a month, +3.6% YTD). USD/BRL 5.488 (+5.1% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.670 (-0.5%); USD/MXN 18.84 (+2.9%).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -2.1% in a month (+10.5% YTD); VIX 20.8. Neutral risk backdrop.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 96.61 $/bbl (+8.0% in a month), Brent 104.18, ULSD 4.547 $/gal (+4.4%), natural gas 2.91 (-12.8%). Higher crude lifts biofuel margins (soybean oil, corn for ethanol) and synthetic-fibre costs (supports cotton), but raises diesel, drying and freight costs. Natural gas drives nitrogen fertilizer costs for next year's corn.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -2.5% in a month, Shanghai Composite -6.1%, Hang Seng -1.9%, yuan +0.5% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 10 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (30%); S&P GSCI -1.1% in a month; gold -5.6%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
